 Sacramento County Opens Three Sandbag Sites For Unincorporated-Area Residents
 Residents should bring a shovel and collect bags before rain falls. Each visit is limited to 20 bags.
 Patch News , Patch Staff 
 Posted Mon, Nov 16, 2026 at 2:51 pm PT Residents in unincorporated Sacramento County whose properties may flood are encouraged to collect sandbags before rain falls. The Sacramento County Department of Water Resources has opened three locations as part of its annual winter preparation.
 The sites are Branch Center, 3847 Branch Center Road, and Orangevale Community Center, 6826 Hazel Ave. A third location is Sacramento Metropolitan Fire Station #116, 7995 Elwyn Ave. The county supplies sand and bags through stormwater utility fees, but residents must bring a shovel and follow a 20-bag limit per visit.
 Residents should replace old sandbags that have deteriorated after sitting in the summer sun. Clearing trash and debris from storm drains before rain can also reduce street flooding. During storms, residents near creeks and streams can use the County ALERT system to monitor rising water in unincorporated areas.

Residents who do not live in unincorporated areas should check with their cities for sandbag information. Residents can find sandbag locations and flood preparedness details online.
 Source: “ County Sandbag Locations Open ” (saccounty.gov)
